acceptance.given: An optional dependency is absent and its declared fallback is available for evaluation.

oracle.expected: The dependency handling execution records the optional dependency as absent, resolves and invokes its declared fallback, and prevents that fallback from authorizing protected work.
forbidden: The absence is treated as undeclared behavior or an unexpected hard failure.
The declared fallback is bypassed, contradicted, unresolved, or replaced by another behavior.
oracle.observable: The validator result or execution record identifies the absent dependency, declared fallback, fallback resolution, and protected-work authorization status.

acceptance.then: The optional-absence path executes the declared resolvable fallback and exposes its result without protected-work authorization.
acceptance.when: Execute the repository skill-authoring implementation validation against a fixture or dependency configuration where the optional dependency is unavailable, then inspect its structured result.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select the optional-dependency absence behavior case and make the optional dependency unavailable; fail if the declared fallback is not resolved and invoked or if the result permits protected-work authorization.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Validate and execute the declared fallback when an optional dependency is absent, while preserving the protected-work authorization boundary.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Reverting restores the prior validator behavior; no persisted schema or database state changes are required.

slice_hint.state_transition: optional dependency absent -> declared fallback resolved -> fallback executed without protected authorization -> structured result available
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The targeted implementation validation command passes only when the optional absence is represented by the declared fallback execution and protected-work authorization remains denied.
